solution: Track the sequence from nitrobenzene. (1) \(Br_{2}/FeBr_{3}\): the nitro group is a meta director, giving 3-bromonitrobenzene (1 Br). (4) \(Br_{2}/H_{2}O\): the strongly activating \(-NH_{2}\) group brominates every free position ortho and para to itself, i.e. C-2, C-4 and C-6, giving 2,3,4,6-tetrabromoaniline (4 Br). Product (P) is pentabromobenzene (Br at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6), i.e. the tetrabromo ring plus the new Br, a total of \(5\) bromine atoms.

Successive ionisation enthalpies rise gradually while electrons come from the valence shell, then jump sharply once the valence shell is empty and the next electron must come from the noble-gas core.

Here \(IE_1 = 800\), \(IE_2 = 2427\), \(IE_3 = 3658\) and \(IE_4 = 25024\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\). The first three rise by factors of about 3 and 1.5, but \(IE_4\) is nearly seven times \(IE_3\). So the atom has exactly three valence electrons, and it belongs to group 13 (these are boron's values).

Group 2 would show the jump after \(IE_2\), group 14 after \(IE_4\). (The fifth value, 32824, is larger than the fourth, as each successive ionisation enthalpy must be; boron's fifth is about 32 830 \(\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\).)

In all three complexes nickel is \(Ni^{2+}\), a \(d^{8}\) ion.

Unpaired electrons: for an octahedral \(d^{8}\) ion the configuration is \(t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}\) whatever the field strength, because the two \(e_{g}\) electrons must occupy the two separate \(e_{g}\) orbitals - so both \([Ni(en)_{3}]^{2+}\) and \([Ni(NH_{3})_{6}]^{2+}\) have 2 unpaired electrons. For tetrahedral \([NiCl_{4}]^{2-}\) the configuration is \(e^{4}t_{2}^{4}\), which again leaves 2 unpaired electrons. So the count is 2, 2, 2.

Frequency of absorption is proportional to the splitting energy \(\Delta\). Ligand field strength runs \(en > NH_{3} > Cl^{-}\), and in addition \(\Delta_{t} \approx \frac{4}{9}\Delta_{o}\), so a tetrahedral chloro complex has by far the smallest splitting. Hence \(\Delta\) and therefore the absorption frequency follow \((A) > (C) > (B)\).

The matching option is '2, 2, 2 and \((A) > (C) > (B)\)'.

Only water and acid leave the beaker, so the leftover acid is now contained in half the original volume, \(400\ mL\). Molar conductivity \(\Lambda_{m} = \kappa/c = 1.14943/50 = 0.022989\ S\,m^{2}\,mol^{-1}\). Converting, \(1\ S\,m^{2} = 10^{3}\ mS \times 10^{2}\ dm^{2} = 10^{5}\ mS\,dm^{2}\), so \(\Lambda_{m} = 2298.9\ mS\,dm^{2}\,mol^{-1} = 23 \times 10^{2}\ mS\,dm^{2}\,mol^{-1}\).

\(MgCl_{2}\) dissociates into three ions, so with degree of dissociation \(\alpha = 0.8\) the van't Hoff factor is \(i = 1 + \alpha(n-1) = 1 + 0.8 \times 2 = 2.6\). The mole fraction of solute is \(2.6/(2.6 + 55.56) = 0.044704\). By Raoult's law the lowered vapour pressure is \(p = p^{\circ}(1 - x_{solute}) = 50 \times (1 - 0.044704) = 47.76\) mm Hg, which is 48 mm Hg to the nearest integer.
